assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the two reviewed items curated on tomozaki:hinami-haruka@light-novel at basis_commit, each read in full: #bounded-character-dossier, the canonical B-scope Hinami Haruka bounded character dossier (INDEPENDENT_BOUNDED_LITERARY_SCOPE_PASS, maturity BOUNDED_INDIVIDUAL_LITERARY_ROLE) over the locked Japanese V01-V12 with story-local V06.5/V08.5, whose positive person evidence is the nine handles HH-E01 to HH-E09 in V08.5, V09, V11 and V12, with earlier bucket cells retained as unknown rather than absence findings; and #bounded-reconstruction-model, the canonical derived-use model TOMOZAKI_HARUKA_B05_MODEL_V1, marked do_not_use_as_primary_literary_authority, which derives from the dossier and is not used as literary evidence. The supporting character implementation review, the supporting literary evidence manifest, the additional-three model integration review and evidence packet, the readings and the ledgers (CS-HAR-01, CS section 13.3/19, REL section 17.1) are not curated on this subject and are not evidence here. Much of Haruka's V11-V12 conduct is seen through Fumiya's or Aoi's narration. No adaptation, performed voice, reception or post-V12 material is in scope.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The model's seven selectors: HH_CHILDHOOD_PLAY and HH_RETROSPECTIVE_SHARED_GAME (V08.5 retrospective scenes inside a later frame, not dated by package order), HH09_FAMILY_INTRO (V09 restaurant), HH11_FIRST_CONTACT, HH11_INQUIRY and HH11_SISTER_APPEAL (V11), and HH12_READING_RELAY (V12, ending with the departure DM and Fumiya's found reply). Her exact current age is not established; earlier volumes are unknown cells; nothing after V12 is established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The dossier's account, that Haruka makes an admired example productive through her own effort and is destabilized when that example becomes unavailable (opening and sections 4-5), rests on her own V11 reports of being the least clever sister whose strength was energy, of school becoming frightening and of Aoi's 'watch me' offer (HH-E04, p-0019), and is operationalized as model mechanisms HM1-HM6. C is rejected because the dossier disclaims the broad interior of a principal monograph, the discovery row claims no psychology, and the model rates new balances of caution, curiosity, recognition and pressure as weaker. E is rejected because the mechanism is tested against six named rival readings (section 8) across four volumes.

Seven clocked selectors run from childhood play to the V12 relay, and the dossier separates scene date, disclosure frame and person-specific access (section 1). C is rejected because the childhood and middle-school states are retrospective scenes or Haruka's own reports rather than independently witnessed development, each later state rests on one or two windows, her age is not established, and durable independence, school-role continuation and later reaction are open (section 9). E is rejected because the states are located and kept distinct, including the reversal of game skill between the two V08.5 scenes.

Register is described rather than quoted: nervous formality in the V09 introduction (HH-E03), a direct LINE refusal with an Instagram alternative (HH-E04), game teasing (HH-E02), a tearful plea (HH-E06) and a practical DM (HH-E09); the model lists this repertoire and generates no freeform Japanese, and the only quoted fragment is the incomplete 'チー…' (section 3). D is rejected because the curated items quote almost no speech, the discovery row claims no speech dimension, and the model states that idiolect, habitual frequencies and delivery are unestablished. NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because distinct registers are located by scene.

Ordinary acts are located: inviting Aoi to Atafami, winning, teaching a dodge's name and teasing (V08.5 part0015 P106-213), a polite restaurant introduction (V09 part0023), and choosing cheese dakgalbi with Kikuchi and reporting cheesecake with her sister (V11 p-0023). C is rejected because the dossier denies an exclusive favorite, a household routine or a diet, and school and home routines are not established. E is rejected because several located acts show her own play, preference and initiative.

The section 7 recipient table gives distinct conduct and a limit for seven recipients or fields (Nagisa in childhood play, Aoi in shared play, Aoi as model, her mother, Fumiya, Kikuchi and the V12 manuscript and peers), and the model's selectors gate recipient familiarity, channel and knowledge, including the heard P239 versus inward P240 split in Fumiya's speech. B is rejected because most recipients rest on one window, her relationship to Yoko is known only through her own report, and her later reaction to the covert inquiry and negotiated family history are open. D is rejected because recipient-dependent variation is explicit and source-located.

Haruka is never a focal consciousness: her inner states come through her own addressed reports (HH-E04, HH-E06), Aoi's narration of her expression and tears (HH-E02, HH-E08) and Fumiya's observation, and the dossier warns that Aoi's reading of her expression is not Haruka's exhaustive inner account and that Fumiya cannot determine every cause of her tears (sections 1 and 5). D is rejected because no Haruka focalization exists and the dossier disclaims a broad interior. NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because direct self-reports of fear, unease and not knowing what to do are located.

Pressure behavior is located: stepping back and gripping a personal alarm before an unfamiliar boy (V11 p-0019), interrupting Fumiya's attempt to stop Kikuchi's answer (p-0023), and pressing the manuscript on Aoi after an initial refusal (V12 p-0022 P151-226). C is rejected because these are single episodes with no sustained interpersonal conflict, and the dossier keeps her V12 urging distinct from a coercive design and leaves future responses open. E is rejected because three distinct located modes exist.

No normative reasoning by Haruka is located in the curated items. The dossier's ethical distinctions (participation versus informed consent, sincerity versus pressure, Aoi owing no perpetual perfection) are its own analysis of her acts, and the model has no ethical-deliberation mechanism. Nothing is established either way; this is a gap in the evidence, not evidence that she lacks moral reasoning.

Play is located in two V08.5 scenes: turning Aoi into the comic great demon king while cheering Nagisa (part0013 P1-57), and later teasing Aoi for studying too much and protesting the 'returning demon king' (part0015 P106-213). C is rejected because play is located only in the retrospective sister scenes and no humor style is analysed beyond local teasing. E is rejected because play has its own agency and is analysed against a designed-rescue reading.

The dossier is an independently accepted B-scope account with nine handles over every positive band (V08.5, V09, V11, V12), and the model binds the dossier's exact bytes and hash. C is rejected because the dossier disclaims principal-monograph coverage, many V11-V12 acts are mediated through other narrators, and open source questions remain on durable independence, later reaction to the covert inquiry, family history and school-role continuation (section 9). E is rejected because every positive band has located windows.

Affirmative limits are located: the LINE refusal bounds her offered access (HH-E04); Aoi's objection to unannounced family contact gives the covert route a cost (p-0030 P549-560); visible shock and tears bound the invited inquiry (HH-E05); a week without reply is shown (p-0028 P199-200); and her own statement that she does not know what to do exposes dependence despite her achievement (HH-E06). B is rejected because several limits are epistemic (motive for silence, rescue intent, durable effect) and each rests on one scene. D is rejected because the limits are explicit and located.

Each selector binds a clock and an access ceiling: V08.5 package order is not story date, the V09 observer age estimate is not her age, Fumiya's P240 qualification is unheard, V12 p-0022 is Aoi's private reader access, and later family knowledge cannot be redistributed by saying 'the family knows'. B is rejected because her age, the retrospective dates and her later state are open and earlier volumes are unknown cells. D is rejected because clock and knowledge controls are explicit for every selector.

scenario_readiness.note: The model generates no freeform Japanese and no exact unheard sentence, the curated items quote almost no speech, and the discovery row claims no speech dimension. CONDITIONAL would treat a register list as a voice. NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the evidence explicitly bounds voice.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One of the selectors HH_CHILDHOOD_PLAY to HH12_READING_RELAY, with V08.5 retrospective states dated by their frame rather than package order, and nothing after the V12 departure DM.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Only attested recipients in their represented standing: Nagisa and Aoi in sister play, Aoi as model, her mother as reported, Fumiya as an unfamiliar then partially trusted older student, Kikuchi and Mizusawa at the food court, and the V12 delivery peers.
setting_constraints: Ordinary sister play, family introduction, first contact with channel choice, an invited inquiry, a sister-directed appeal or reading and relay only
No therapy, crisis, romance, vocation, school-role continuation or durable family repair
Who heard or read what and any expressed refusal must be supplied; output would be a labeled hypothetical range, never an observed canonical event

scenario_readiness.note: The dossier states that era-conditioned constraints are possible but exact new behavior is not established and that none of its scenario notes is a blinded prediction test (section 8), and the model places severe unfamiliar crisis, family therapy, later independence, vocation and broad biography outside its field. CONDITIONAL would generate novel contexts from a B-scope account with no focal interior. NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the evidence explicitly bounds transfer.

conditions: One named selector (HH_RETROSPECTIVE_SHARED_GAME, HH09_FAMILY_INTRO, HH11_FIRST_CONTACT or HH11_INQUIRY) with its recipient familiarity and actual channel.
Recipient, setting, request, shared history and any refusal are supplied; no exclusive favorite, routine or age is invented.
Output is a qualitative prose range with local register noted, not generated dialogue.
scenario_readiness.note: Ordinary play, food choice and a polite introduction are located, and HM1 and HM3 model play and selective access, which the model names among its firmer fields. READY is rejected because household and school routines, favorites and exact age are not established and the model requires selector, recipient, channel and history. NOT_READY is rejected because ordinary play and contact choices are model-admitted and source-located.
No deliberation by Haruka is located, and the curated items neither model nor bound it. Nothing is established either way.

No romantic conduct of Haruka's appears in the curated items. The only romance-adjacent fact is her hearing Fumiya say he likes Aoi, which the model bounds as her knowledge of his speech, not as evidence about her own romantic behavior. Nothing is established either way.

Her school-council presidency is reported (HH-E04, HH-E06) but never shown, and the dossier denies an adult political vocation, universal leadership skill or the quality of her administration. CONDITIONAL would generate council conduct from a report. NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the achievement and its limits are located.

known_limits.statement: The text offers possible concern for Aoi as a reason for Haruka's Atafami invitation but does not settle it; a consciously designed rescue exceeds the evidence.
Haruka's middle-school presidency and campaign work are her own reports to Fumiya and Aoi; no administration, leadership skill or vocation is shown.
Haruka refuses LINE as private and offers Instagram; agreeing to talk does not grant every channel, audience or reuse of her family testimony.
Haruka asks Kikuchi for her view and stops Fumiya's interruption, then is visibly hurt; participation is not informed anticipation or permission to publish her words.
A week after the food court Haruka has not replied to Fumiya; that is a finite interval, not a refusal, punishment or diagnosis.
Haruka reads the manuscript independently and presses it on Aoi after Aoi refused it; sincerity does not erase pressure, and a later benefit is not prior consent.
Haruka's V12 DM reports Aoi's unsteady departure; it does not transmit Aoi's private p-0022 reading or create a supervision role.
Fumiya's 'as one person' qualification is inward; Haruka hears only his liking for Aoi and cannot hold a final romantic classification.
Haruka's exact current age is not established; the V09 observer estimate is not a measurement.
Durable independent value, family repair and her full later reaction to the covert inquiry are open source questions.
Earlier bucket cells marked unknown are not findings that Haruka was absent from those volumes.
No idiolect, habitual frequencies or acoustic delivery is established; no freeform Japanese or blind accuracy is validated.
Nothing after the V12 boundary is evidenced.
